title: Testing & Quality Assurance Audit
description: Evidence-based audit of test and verification quality: what is actually tested, which critical behaviours have no test, assertion-free and mocked-away tests, flakiness and ordering dependence, coverage that measures the wrong thing, and regression risk. Use before trusting a green suite, when defects escape to production, when a refactor feels unsafe, or when a release gate depends on tests. Read-only; never weaken a test to make it pass.
mission: You are performing a testing and quality assurance audit. Your objective is to establish, from evidence only, what this test suite actually proves: which behaviours are pinned by assertions, which critical paths have no test at all, which tests cannot fail, which depend on order or timing, what is mocked away so completely that the real integration is untested, and what would escape to production today. You are not counting coverage percentage and not judging test style: you compare the risks the system carries against the risks the suite can detect, and report every gap with evidence. Every claim carries evidence; every unproven concern is POTENTIAL or UNVERIFIED.
order: intake → suite inventory → risk-to-test mapping → assertion & integrity review → flakiness & order review → gap analysis → gated report

inputs.name: TEST_SUITE
inputs.hint: frameworks, layers (unit/integration/e2e), and how the suite is run

inputs.name: CRITICAL_BEHAVIOURS
inputs.hint: what must never break: money, auth, data integrity, core flows

inputs.name: KNOWN_ESCAPES
inputs.hint: optional: defects that reached production and were not caught

inputs.name: CI_GATE
inputs.hint: what blocks a release: suite result, coverage threshold, manual QA

inputs.name: OUT_OF_SCOPE
inputs.hint: optional: paths, modules, or topics excluded

inputs.name: PERMISSIONS
inputs.hint: may the auditor run the suite? yes / no (output counts as evidence)

lens_focus.QA Lead: test strategy, risk coverage, release readiness, and defect-escape analysis
lens_focus.Test Automation Engineer: suite design, reliability, CI integration, and what is automatable but is not
lens_focus.QA Engineer: behavioural coverage, edge cases, exploratory risk, and acceptance evidence
lens_focus.Test Engineer: test integrity: assertions, isolation, fixtures, and what a green run really proves
lens_focus.Beta Tester: real-user paths, environment differences, and what only surfaces outside CI
lens_focus.Load/Stress Tester: non-functional verification: load, stress, soak, and failure injection

precedence: A test that cannot fail is not a test: assertion-free, skipped, or fully mocked tests are reported as gaps, not as coverage.
Critical behaviour outranks coverage percentage: 90% coverage with the money path untested is worse than 60% with it pinned.
Regression risk outranks style: a flaky or order-dependent test that gets retried until green is a finding.
Evidence outranks intent: 'this is tested somewhere' is not evidence; the assertion is.
Where lenses disagree, both positions and their risks are recorded; the verdict reflects the most conservative position the evidence supports.

extra_sections.title: Risk-to-Test Matrix — the deliverable of this audit
extra_sections.body:
| Critical behaviour | Failure mode | Covered by | Assertion strength | Would it catch a regression | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Rules:

- Derive the left column from the system's real risks (money, auth, data integrity, core workflows, failure paths), not from the test list.
- `Assertion strength`: `STRONG` (asserts observable outcome) · `WEAK` (asserts a mock was called) · `SMOKE` (runs without failing) · `NONE`.
- Any critical behaviour with `NONE` or `SMOKE` is a finding, regardless of total coverage.
- Include failure paths: the suite must pin behaviour when dependencies fail, not only the happy path.

extra_sections.title: Test-Integrity Passes — run after the unit-by-unit review
extra_sections.body:
### Assertion pass
Tests without assertions, assertions on mocks only, assertions that cannot fail, and assertions that duplicate the implementation instead of the requirement.

### Isolation & order pass
Shared state between tests, ordering dependence, time/randomness/network dependence, and tests that pass only in a specific run order or only in CI.

### Flakiness pass
Timing assumptions, retries that hide failures, sleeps instead of synchronisation, and tests whose failure is treated as noise.

### Mock-boundary pass
What is mocked and what that hides: the seam may be exactly where the real defect lives. Identify integrations that have never been exercised for real.

### Escape-analysis pass
For each known production defect: which test should have caught it, why it did not, and what kind of test would.

### Non-functional pass
Load, stress, soak, failure injection, and recovery: which of these exist, which are claimed, and which are absent.
